Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0002] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a money-related function, inspect ledgerly/money.py and existing helpers (line_total, invoice_total) to reuse ZERO, to_money, and round_money rather than raw arithmetic.
[ace-0004] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Before writing a new function, read sibling modules (e.g. payments.py, subscriptions.py) to mirror their BillingError codes, message formats, and validation ordering so the new code is consistent with the codebase.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When computing a weighted average or division of money, wrap the final result in round_money; returning an unrounded Decimal division fails review even if visible tests pass.
[ace-0005] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) since True/False are ints in Python and would otherwise pass a positive-integer check.
## domain_facts
[ace-0001] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, all monetary values must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
[ace-0006] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, BillingError(code, detail) is the standard error type; existing codes include invalid_state, non_positive_amount, before_start, and float_amount (raised by to_money for non-Decimal/float inputs).

item.content: For date/time functions in ledgerly, normalize inputs with clock.ensure_utc (which raises BillingError for naive/non-datetime values) and mirror sibling modules like subscriptions.current_period for validation ordering and error codes.

When computing the next occurrence of a periodic event, use floor division ((after - start) // length) and then bump by one period if the result is not strictly after `after`; also handle after < start explicitly so the start itself is never returned as a renewal.

In ledgerly, Subscription has started_at (datetime) and period_days (int); renewals occur every period_days from started_at, and the start is not itself a renewal. Invalid period_days should raise BillingError (e.g. code invalid_period).
